newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila call loan rates steady amid liquid market.
newsitem.headline: Manila call loan rates steady amid liquid market.

text.p: *Volume lower at 6.397 bln from 7.484 bln pesos
Philippine interbank call loan rates were unchanged on Thursday at an average of 10.53125 percent since the Central Bank kept a floor on interest rates amid high liquidity, traders said.
The Central Bank had been borrowing at an overnight rate of 10.50 percent, they said.
Done rates were wedged from 10.625 to 10.53125 percent, with 22 lenders and 16 borrowers.
"There's still so much money in the system. It's been at these levels because of the cut in reserves," a foreign bank trader said. Banks' requirement reserves were cut effective Friday.

Traders said liquidity also increased because most banks had not reinvested their money in term reverse repos after the government decided to impose a 20 percent tax on these bills starting January 2.
Due to the very liquid market, most banks continued to bid for T-bills, traders said.
"There was very little selling. Banks were just servicing clients' maturities," a trader said.
A Reuter poll of five institutions showed banks were quoting bid rates of 10.90 to 11.05 percent; 11.15 to 11.25 percent for six months; and 11.40 to 11.60 for one year.
